headline: New computational methods advance RNA structure prediction and design
label: Rna Structure Modeling Methods
summary: Recent preprints apply deep learning and linear-time probability methods to RNA folding, 3D prediction, and nanopore tRNA reads.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational modeling of RNA structure, with several preprints adding learned or probabilistic components. A GVP-Transformer framework addresses RNA inverse folding using geometric structure potentials and a new 3D RNA structure dataset. LinearCapR computes per-nucleotide structural-context probabilities in linear time without base-pair span limits, with reported improvements for multiloops and long-range pairing. A Kaggle blind code competition on RNA 3D structure prediction (1700+ teams, 43 unreleased structures) reports that its top template-based pipeline matched CASP16 winners. tRNAZAP classifies native tRNA nanopore ionic current signals at isodecoder resolution. Two items, VINE phylogenetics and BABAPPAlign protein alignment, fall outside RNA but share the learned-scoring theme. What is new is the move toward per-nucleotide and sequence-to-structure inference driven directly by learned models and raw experimental signal.
